category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain is recognized as a complex experience consisting of two primary dimensions: the sensory aspect and the [___] (emotional) aspect.
back:
• Affective aspect
• Imparts the unpleasant quality to pain
• Often holds greater clinical significance than the sensory component

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 35-year-old female with chronic lower back pain presents with insomnia, irritability, and social withdrawal. Physical exams and imaging are normal. What is the most likely underlying psychological morbidity?
back:
• Depressive Disorder
• Seen in over 75% of chronic backache patients
• Presents with somatic symptoms like anorexia and lethargy

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the pharmacological mechanism by which Tricyclic Antidepressants (e.g., Amitriptyline) alleviate chronic pain.
back:
• Blocks biogenic amine uptake (Serotonin and Noradrenaline)
• Enhances inhibitory action on spinal pain transmission pathways
• Modifies the affective component of pain

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast the 'time-contingent' dosing method with 'pain-contingent' dosing in the management of chronic opioid use.
back:
• Time-contingent: Fixed regular intervals; decreases addictive potential and pain behavior
• Pain-contingent: Dosing based on intensity; reinforces the 'sick role' and increases addiction risk

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Describe the clinical benefit of using anxiolytics like Benzodiazepines in acute pain management.
back:
• Relieves feelings of impending disaster/dread
• Lowers the requirement for higher doses of post-surgical analgesic medications

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Chronic pain associated with underlying negative emotions like unexpressed anger or frustration typically manifests in the [___] groups of muscles.
back:
• Extensor muscle groups
• Commonly affects the back, cranium, and precordium

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient experiences severe, prolonged pain that does not follow anatomical nerve distributions and arose after a significant environmental stressor, without organic cause. Identify this condition.
back:
• Psychogenic Pain Disorder
• Mechanism similar to hallucinations or dreams
• Inconsistent with the anatomical nervous system

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the role of 'Imaginative Inattention' as a cognitive strategy for pain control.
back:
• Focuses on thoughts incompatible with pain
• Example: Imagining a quiet beach
• Transforms the context of the sensation to reduce emotional distress

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast 'Active Coping' with 'Passive Coping' strategies in chronic pain patients.
back:
• Active: Engaging in physical exercise/PT; clearing the mind of worries
• Passive: Social withdrawal; relying on medication for immediate relief; resting

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Identify three common somatic gastrointestinal expressions of depression often seen in chronic pain patients.
back:
• Constipation
• Indigestion (often described as 'gases')
• Anorexia (loss of appetite)

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain is considered a multidimensional experience consisting of two primary aspects: sensory and [___].
back:
• Affective (emotional)
• This aspect imparts the unpleasant quality to pain.
• It is often of greater clinical significance than the sensory component in chronic cases.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 35-year-old female with persistent jaw pain describes it as "dull and disgusting." She reports insomnia, irritability, and suicidal ideation despite multiple analgesics. State the likely underlying diagnosis.
back:
• Depressive Disorder
• Over 75% of chronic pain patients (e.g., backache) exhibit clinical depression.
• Requires antidepressants (TCAs) and psychosocial support rather than just analgesics.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Describe the mechanism by which tricyclic antidepressants like Imipramine alleviate chronic pain symptoms.
back:
• Blocks biogenic amine uptake (Serotonin and Noradrenaline).
• Enhances inhibitory action on spinal pain transmission pathways.
• Modulates the affective-motivational dimension of the pain experience.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast the primary emotional correlate and management focus between acute and chronic pain states.
back:
• Acute Pain: Correlated with anxiety/dread; managed with reassurance and anxiolytics.
• Chronic Pain: Correlated with depression/social withdrawal; managed with antidepressants and cognitive strategies.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the 'time-contingent' dosing method used in operant techniques for chronic opioid users.
back:
• Medication is provided at regular time intervals regardless of pain intensity.
• Replaces 'pain-contingent' (as-needed) dosing.
• Reduces addictive potential and decreases reinforced "pain behaviors."

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain that is prolonged, severe, inconsistent with anatomical nerve distribution, and lacks a structural cause is termed [___].
back:
• Psychogenic Pain Disorder
• Often triggered by environmental stress.
• Mechanism is similar to dreams or hallucinations rather than noxious stimuli.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient avoids work claiming severe pain but is capable of watching television and reading for hours without distress. Identify this behavioral phenomenon.
back:
• Sick Role (Pain Behavior)
• Characterized by avoidance based on fear of pain.
• Involves reinforcement of passive learning and selective functional disability.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: How does 'imaginative inattention' function as a cognitive strategy for managing chronic pain?
back:
• Patient visualizes a scene incompatible with pain (e.g., a quiet beach).
• Involves "transformation of context" where pain is re-imagined in a different setting.
• Diverts cognitive resources away from the pain experience.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Distinguish between active and passive coping strategies used by patients with chronic pain syndromes.
back:
• Active: Physical exercise, physical therapy, and clearing the mind of worries.
• Passive: Restricting social activities and relying on medication for immediate, temporary relief.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Identify the demographic group most prone to chronic pain and the typical temporal pattern of such pain.
back:
• Demographic: Females (twice as prone as males).
• Pattern: Virtually continuous while awake, but characteristically never wakes the patient from sleep.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
coreConcept: Mechanism of TCAs in Chronic Pain
front: In the management of chronic pain, Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs) like Amitriptyline relieve symptoms by blocking biogenic amine uptake, which enhances the inhibitory action of [___] on spinal pain transmission pathways.
back:
• Serotonin
• Nor-adrenaline (Norepinephrine)

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 45-year-old female presents with persistent, "dull and disgusting" jaw pain for 8 months. Physical exam and dental X-rays are normal. She reports irritability, insomnia, and loss of interest in her family. Identify the most likely underlying psychiatric diagnosis.
back:
• Depressive Disorder (Clinical Depression)
• Studies show >75% of chronic pain patients have comorbid depression.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the role of 'Imaginative Inattention' as a cognitive strategy in pain management.
back:
• Patient focuses on thoughts incompatible with pain.
• Examples include imagining a quiet place or transforming the context (e.g., imagining pain occurs in a different, safe situation).

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast 'Pain-contingent' dosing with 'Time-contingent' dosing in chronic opioid therapy.
back:
• Pain-contingent: Medication given 'as needed' (PRN), reinforcing pain behavior and increasing addiction risk.
• Time-contingent: Medication given at regular intervals regardless of pain, decreasing disability and addictive potential.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List the four most common anatomical sites for chronic pain associated with psychiatric morbidity.
back:
• Precordium
• Genitals
• Face
• Cranium

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: The condition characterized by chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and excessive pain in response to tactile pressure, often precipitated by psychological stress, is [___].
back: • Fibromyalgia

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient avoids work and physical activity due to fear of pain, yet remains comfortable while watching TV or reading. Explain the behavioral phenomenon occurring here.
back:
• Pain Behavior (Sick Role)
• Involves avoidance based on fear and reinforcement of passive learning.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain why the 'Affective' aspect of pain is often more clinically significant than the 'Sensory' aspect.
back:
• Affective aspect imparts the 'unpleasant' and emotional quality.
• It dictates the patient's reaction, motivation, and attempts at seeking analgesia.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast Active Coping versus Passive Coping strategies in chronic pain syndrome.
back:
• Active: Engaging in exercise, physical therapy, or clearing the mind.
• Passive: Cancelling social activities or taking medication for immediate, short-term relief.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Chronic backache aggravated by unexpressed anger or frustration typically manifests in which specific muscle group?
back: • Extensor group of muscles.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: According to the multidimensional model of pain, the experience consists of a sensory aspect and an [___] aspect, the latter being more clinically significant for its unpleasant quality.
back:
Affective (emotional).
- Determined by past history and state of mind.
- Imparts the 'unpleasant' or 'distressing' quality.
- Influences the cognitive reaction to injury.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient with chronic jaw pain reports insomnia, irritability, and feeling 'fed up' with life. Symptoms are unresponsive to analgesics but improve with family involvement and antidepressants. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?
back:
Depressive Disorder.
- Found in >75% of chronic backache cases.
- Often manifests as somatic symptoms (e.g., indigestion).
- Requires biopsychosocial management rather than just analgesics.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the role of Tricyclic Antidepressants (e.g., Imipramine) in the neurochemical modulation of spinal pain transmission pathways.
back:
Blocks biogenic amine uptake.
- Enhances inhibitory actions of serotonin and noradrenaline.
- Suppresses pain signals at the spinal level.
- Effective for chronic pain even without clinical depression.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast 'Time-contingent' medication dosing with 'Pain-contingent' dosing in the management of chronic opioid therapy.
back:
Time-contingent: Fixed intervals regardless of pain.
- Reduces addictive potential and 'pain behavior'.
- Pain-contingent: Dosing triggered by pain intensity.
- Reinforces the 'sick role' and passive learning.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
coreConcept: Pain Behavior and the Sick Role
front: Describe the typical characteristics of 'Pain Behavior' (Sick Role) in a patient with chronic functional disability.
back:
Avoidance-based lifestyle.
- Fear of pain limits physical/social activity.
- Reinforcement of passive learning.
- Patient is 'fine' during passive tasks (TV) but 'too sick' for work.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain that is prolonged, severe, inconsistent with anatomical distribution, and lacks a demonstrable organic or psychiatric cause is termed [___].
back:
Psychogenic Pain Disorder.
- Mechanism similar to hallucinations or dreams.
- Onset is usually related to environmental stress.
- Often reflects a heightened response to somatic sensations.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 40-year-old female presents with chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and tenderness to tactile pressure precipitated by family stress. Identify this clinical entity.
back:
Fibromyalgia.
- Characterized by widespread pain and fatigue.
- Precipitated by psychological factors and stress.
- Associated with excessive pain response to pressure.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain how 'Imaginative Inattention' is utilized as a cognitive strategy to manage acute distress during painful procedures.
back:
Thinking of incompatible experiences.
- Patient imagines a relaxing, quiet environment.
- Transformation of context (reimagining pain in a safer scenario).
- Diverts cognitive resources away from the noxious stimulus.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Distinguish between 'Active' and 'Passive' coping strategies in the context of chronic pain management.
back:
Active: Physical exercise and clearing bothersome thoughts.
- Passive: Social withdrawal and taking medication for immediate relief.
- Active strategies lead to better functional outcomes.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List the common somatic expressions of depression frequently encountered in chronic pain patients within the Pakistani cultural context.
back:
Somatic Expressions:
- Insomnia and exhaustion.
- Anorexia (loss of appetite).
- Constipation.
- Feelings of 'gases' or indigestion.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: In the multidimensional model of pain, the [___] aspect is of greater clinical significance because it imparts the unpleasant quality to the experience.
back:
The Affective (emotional) aspect.
- Determines the subjective 'unpleasantness' of pain.
- Influenced by past history and 'state of mind'.
- Often more significant than the sensory aspect in chronic cases.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 40-year-old female presents with chronic 'dull' jaw pain, disturbed sleep, and irritability. Physical examination is normal and analgesics have failed. Identify the likely underlying diagnosis and treatment.
back:
Depressive Disorder.
- Masked by somatic symptoms (chronic pain).
- Treatment: Antidepressants (e.g., Amitriptyline) and psychosocial support.
- Common in 75% of patients with chronic backache.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs) like Imipramine alleviate chronic pain within the spinal cord.
back:
Biogenic amine uptake blockade.
- Enhances inhibitory action of Serotonin and Nor-adrenaline.
- Modulates spinal pain transmission pathways.
- Acts as an adjuvant to traditional analgesia.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast 'time-contingent' medication dosing with 'pain-contingent' dosing in the context of chronic opioid management.
back:
Time-contingent vs. Pain-contingent.
- Time-contingent: Fixed intervals; reduces addictive potential and pain behavior.
- Pain-contingent: Taken only when pain peaks; reinforces the 'sick role' and increases addiction risk.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Describe the behavioral pattern known as the 'Sick Role' when pain becomes a learned behavior rather than a symptom.
back:
Avoidance-based unhealthy lifestyle.
- Fear of pain leads to decreased activity.
- Reinforcement of passive learning.
- Patient avoids work but remains active during passive tasks (e.g., watching TV).

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain that is virtually continuous while awake, never wakes the patient from sleep, and is unresponsive to analgesics often involves a site with [___] significance.
back:
Symbolic significance.
- Common sites: Genitals, face, and cranium.
- Often reflects underlying emotional conflicts.
- Key feature of chronic psychogenic-type presentations.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient reports severe, widespread pain and fatigue precipitated by stress, specifically showing excessive pain in response to tactile pressure. Name the most likely clinical entity.
back:
Fibromyalgia.
- Characterized by chronic widespread pain and fatigue.
- Triggered by stress and psychosocial factors.
- Features hypersensitivity to tactile pressure.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Distinguish between 'Active' and 'Passive' coping strategies used by patients in response to chronic pain syndromes.
back:
Active vs. Passive Coping.
- Active: Engaging in exercise, physical therapy, or clearing bothersome thoughts.
- Passive: Restricting social activities or relying strictly on medication for immediate relief.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain how 'Imaginative Inattention' is utilized as a cognitive strategy to manage pain.
back:
Cognitive diversion.
- Thinking about something incompatible with pain (e.g., a quiet beach).
- Transforming context (imagining pain is part of a different, appropriate scenario).
- Reduces the perceived intensity of the affective experience.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Identify the primary emotional correlate of repeated acute pain episodes and its impact on post-surgical recovery.
back:
Anxiety.
- Manifests as a feeling of impending disaster/dread.
- Increases the requirement for post-surgical analgesic medication.
- Managed through reassurance and anxiolytics.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: The [___] aspect of pain is primarily responsible for imparting its unpleasant quality and holds greater clinical significance than the sensory component.
back: • Affective (emotional) aspect. • Determines how the individual perceives and reacts to suffering. • Includes cognitive and motivational dimensions.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 45-year-old male with chronic low back pain for 8 months presents with insomnia, lethargy, and loss of interest in social activities. Physical exam is unremarkable. Name the most likely psychiatric comorbidity.
back: • Depressive Disorder. • Affects over 75% of chronic backache patients. • Manifests via somatic expressions like anorexia and sleep disturbances.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain how Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs), such as Imipramine, contribute to analgesia in chronic pain management.
back: • Block biogenic amine uptake. • Enhance inhibitory action of Serotonin and Noradrenaline. • Modulate spinal pain transmission pathways.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast the anatomical distribution and onset of Psychogenic Pain Disorder with pain resulting from organic somatic lesions.
back: • Psychogenic: Inconsistent with nervous system anatomy; related to environmental stress. • Organic: Follows specific dermatomes or nerve distributions; triggered by noxious stimuli.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Describe the 'Time-Contingent' dosing strategy used in the Operant Technique for managing chronic opioid use.
back: • Medication provided at regular intervals regardless of pain intensity. • Prevents reinforcement of 'pain behavior.' • Reduces addictive potential and improves relief.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
coreConcept: Clinical features of chronic psychogenic pain
front: Chronic pain that is virtually continuous while awake but [___] is a characteristic feature often associated with underlying psychological factors or depressive features.
back: • Never wakes the patient from sleep. • Differentiates psychogenic/affective pain from strictly organic pathology which may interrupt sleep.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient avoids all physical activity due to fear of pain but comfortably watches TV for hours. Identify this pattern of reinforcement and unhealthy lifestyle.
back: • Pain Behaviour (or Sick Role). • Characterized by functional disability and avoidance. • Reinforces passive learning and social withdrawal.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Detail the psychological mechanism by which 'Imaginative Inattention' serves as a cognitive strategy for pain management.
back: • Focuses on thoughts incompatible with pain. • Uses transformation of context (e.g., imagining pain in a safe setting). • Diverts attention away from noxious stimuli.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Distinguish between the primary emotional correlates associated with Acute Pain versus Chronic Pain.
back: • Acute Pain: Associated with Anxiety, dread, and 'impending disaster.' • Chronic Pain: Associated with Depression, low self-esteem, and social withdrawal.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List the three main aspects of the 'Psychology of Pain' that influence a patient's reaction and attempts at analgesia.
back: • Affective (emotional). • Motivational. • Cognitive (the meaning ascribed to the pain).

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
coreConcept: Dual Nature of Pain (Sensory vs. Affective)
front: Pain is conceptualized as having two primary dimensions: the sensory dimension and the [___] dimension, which imparts an unpleasant quality.
back:
* Affective (Emotional) dimension
* Imparts the unpleasant quality
* Determines clinical significance
* Influenced by past history and 'state of mind'.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 45-year-old female with persistent lower back pain for 8 months presents with insomnia, irritability, and social withdrawal. Despite normal imaging, she feels 'fed up with life.' Name the likely psychiatric comorbidity.
back:
* Depressive Disorder
* Found in over 75% of chronic backache patients
* Symptoms: Anorexia, sleep disturbance, irritability
* Often requires TCAs (e.g., Amitriptyline) and counseling.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Explain the pharmacological mechanism of Tricyclic Antidepressants (e.g., Imipramine) in the modulation of chronic pain.
back:
* Blocks biogenic amine uptake (serotonin and noradrenaline)
* Enhances inhibitory action on spinal pain transmission
* Modulates the affective/emotional component of pain
* Useful for psychogenic and chronic pain states.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Contrast the 'time-contingent' medication approach with 'pain-contingent' dosing in the management of chronic opioid use.
back:
* Time-contingent: Regular intervals; reduces addictive potential and pain behavior
* Pain-contingent: Taken when pain spikes; reinforces the sick role
* Time-contingent allows for systematic dose reduction.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List the core components of 'Pain Behavior' seen in patients who have adopted the sick role.
back:
* Functional disabilities and decreased social activities
* Overuse of medications
* Sleep disturbances
* Avoidance based on fear of pain (passive learning).

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: In patients where chronic pain serves as a somatic expression of emotional conflict, the most common site involved is the [___].
back:
* Precordium
* Also common: Face, cranium, and genitals
* Often holds symbolic significance for the patient
* Responds poorly to traditional analgesics.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient presents with severe, prolonged pain that is inconsistent with nervous system anatomy and lacks a noxious stimulus, following major environmental stress. Identify this condition.

* Psychogenic Pain Disorder
* Onset related to environmental stress
* No underlying structural illness
* Mechanism similar to hallucinations or dreams.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain

back:

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain

back:
* Active: Exercise, physical therapy, clearing mind of worries
* Passive: Cancelling social activities, relying on immediate medication for relief
* Passive coping leads to higher disability levels.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List three psychological symptoms frequently seen as somatic expressions of depression in chronic pain patients.
back:
* Insomnia (dyssomnias)
* Anorexia (weight loss)
* Lethargy or exhaustion
* Also: Constipation and 'gases'.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Pain is a multidimensional experience consisting of two primary aspects: the sensory-discriminative dimension and the [___] dimension.
back: The affective (emotional) dimension. It imparts the unpleasant quality to pain. It is often of greater clinical significance than the sensory component.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A 35-year-old female presents with chronic 'dull and disgusting' jaw pain, insomnia, and irritability. Investigations show no organic pathology. Identify the likely underlying psychosocial diagnosis.
back: Depressive Disorder. Chronic pain is frequently a somatic expression of depression. Management requires antidepressants and psychosocial support rather than simple analgesics.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: List the defining characteristics of Psychogenic Pain Disorder.
back: No organic noxious stimulus or structural pathology. Inconsistent with anatomical nervous system distribution. Onset typically related to environmental stress.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A condition characterized by chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and excessive sensitivity to tactile pressure precipitated by psychological stress is [___].
back: Fibromyalgia. It involves a heightened response to pressure. Often requires a combination of stress management and physical therapy.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: A patient reports being in too much pain to attend work but is comfortably able to watch television for hours. Identify this clinical behavioral pattern.
back: Pain Behavior (Sick Role). Characterized by avoidance based on fear. Reinforced by passive learning and functional disability.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain
front: Differentiate between 'Imaginative Inattention' and 'Attention Diversion' as cognitive strategies for pain control.
back: Imaginative Inattention: Thinking of something incompatible with pain (e.g., relaxing on a beach). Attention Diversion: Engaging in a demanding mental task (e.g., counting or reading) to shift focus.

Depressive Disorder.

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain

category: At end of module the students will learn the psychosocial aspects of pain which will help in understanding the complex and multidimensional nature of pain

- Virtually continuous while awake but disappears during sleep.

- Medication given at regular intervals regardless of pain intensity.
- Allows for systematic dose reduction.
